instruction: chi cannot tell a missing URL parameter from an empty one: `URLParam`, `URLParamFromCtx` and `(*Context).URLParam` all return "" for both, and `RouteContext` returns a nil `*Context` when the request carries no routing context. Make both explicit, comma-ok style: change `URLParam(r *http.Request, key string) string`, `URLParamFromCtx(ctx context.Context, key string) string` and `(x *Context) URLParam(key string) string` (context.go) to return `(string, bool)`, where the bool reports whether the routing context has a parameter with that key ("", false when it does not, or when there is no routing context), and change `RouteContext(ctx context.Context) *Context` to return `(*Context, bool)` (ok reports whether a routing context is present; the pointer is nil exactly when ok is false). Update every caller in the module (mux, tree, the middleware package and all tests): callers that only need the value discard the bool (`v, _ := ...`); a call used inside a larger expression (a `fmt.Sprintf`/`fmt.Fprintf` argument, `[]byte(...)`, a string concatenation, a comparison) must be hoisted into its own `name, _ := ...` statement just before the statement that uses it, keeping the evaluation order of the arguments; callers that guarded on `rctx != nil` may keep doing so. Do not add single-result helpers or wrappers (in tests either), and do not change `URLParams`/`RouteParams` or the `_examples` modules. Behavior must not change.
gold_tool: build_deep.py deephard go recipe: context.go declarations by explicit edit; callers from go build/go test compile errors: `x := f()` binds `x, _`, other uses hoisted into `<key-named var>, _ := f()` statements at go/ast statement positions (deephard_astq.go); gofmt (go1.25)
change: change four accessors' results T -> (T, bool) (URLParam, URLParamFromCtx, Context.URLParam, RouteContext); callers in expression contexts are hoisted into named statements
notes: Hoisted names come from the parameter key ("hubID" -> hubID, "*" -> wildcard); several calls in one fmt.Sprintf are hoisted in argument order.
